unexpectedGrant.finding: At 16:43:27.171 (between C probe at 16:43:14 and D harness at 16:43:50), TCC wrote: Update Access Record: kTCCServiceScreenCapture for the external daemon path to Allowed (System Set). This is a separate grant to the external daemon subject (its own path), NOT an inheritance of com.codebridge.app. Most plausibly a system prompt triggered by the C probe SCK call was answered with Allow (HUMAN ACTION). The spike protocol required keeping any daemon entry OFF.
unexpectedGrant.consequence: D harness Screen showed Allowed (System Set) with a real 1800x1169 capture — via the daemon's own new grant, not the App grant. AX and Input remained denied for both C and D.

inheritanceVerdict: NO_APP_GRANT_INHERITANCE: the external daemon resolves to its own path-based TCC subject, never com.codebridge.app. Before any grant, C was denied on all three services. AX and Input stayed denied throughout C and D.

grantSource.finding: The 16:43:27.171 grant to the external daemon path was written by SecurityPrivacyExtension PID 48048 via TCCAccessSetInternal (msgID=48048.9, REPLY success). System Settings had been open since 16:43:17. This is a Settings-UI-driven write — i.e., a HUMAN ACTION in the Screen Recording pane answered a system prompt for the external codebridged entry with Allow (either automatically presented from the C probe SCK call, or toggled manually). It is NOT an inheritance of com.codebridge.app and NOT a tool/script write.

summary.inheritance: NO_APP_GRANT_INHERITANCE — external daemon resolves to its own path-based TCC subject; before any grant, C was denied on all three services (real SCK -3801, AX trusted=false, Input preflight=false); AX and Input stayed denied throughout C and D.
summary.anomaly: A Screen Recording grant was written to the EXTERNAL daemon path itself at 16:43:27 (between C and D), making D's Screen probe succeed with Allowed (System Set) — via the daemon's own grant, not the App's. Per the spike protocol, the external daemon entry should have stayed OFF.

humanConfirmation.report: 弹出后我点了允许 — the user confirmed they clicked Allow on the system prompt for the external codebridged entry, explaining the 16:43:27 grant. This was an explicit human grant to the external daemon subject, not an inheritance and not a tool write.

finalJudgment.independentDaemonTccBoundary: PASS — before any grant, the external launchd-owned daemon was DENIED on all three Computer services (real SCK -3801, AX trusted=false, Input preflight=false), with its own path-based TCC subject, never com.codebridge.app. No App-grant inheritance.
finalJudgment.f2TopologySpike: PASS_WITH_D_SCREEN_CONTAMINATION — D no longer inherits App grants (subject = external daemon), but D inherits the external daemon's own grant: the D-Screen Allowed row was taken after the user explicitly granted Screen Recording to the external entry (16:43:27, TCCAccessSetInternal), so it is contaminated for isolation purposes. AX and Input stayed denied for C and D throughout; pre-grant Screen-DENY was directly observed at C. A clean D Screen=DENIED row under App-only grants is required from the production F2 matrix. An external daemon Computer grant is itself a dangerous configuration — codified as DAEMON_COMPUTER_TCC_MUST_BE_NONE.
finalJudgment.architectureAmendment: RECOMMENDED — proceed with ARCHITECTURE_AMENDMENT_V2_F2 (external daemon topology, option b).
finalJudgment.productionNote: The spike also exposed a UX consequence: an external daemon requesting SCK triggers a real system prompt; production must ensure the daemon never requests Computer permissions, or users can grant them directly — IPC policy must fail closed on daemon-side Computer capability regardless.
